doc.title: Scott Yanow interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, October 22, 2021

title: Musicians' reactions to reviews
summary: Praise and complaints from musicians are about equal and track whether the review was favorable.

story.theme_name: Where jazz stands today: young players, rock, and the audience
story.community_name: Critics, polls and the jazz press

blocks.x: What kind of feedback over the years have you received from the artists you review? Let me rephrase. Are you more likely to get contacted by aggravated musicians who didn’t like what you wrote rather than people thanking you for your review?

Pretty even, really. When you are a jazz critic you have to know that if a musician compliments you that means if you liked their last record. That means if they say you are a great writer that means you wrote a great review for them. And if you wrote a negative review then you’re a bum. Like, so you can’t really take their opinions too seriously, much of the time, unless it’s someone you know and they’re being really honest about it. I mean it’s kind of funny, there was one saxophonist who because of the Internet you know reviews stay up there forever. And I wrote something for the All Music Guide maybe in 1995 on him, and he has criticized the review I wrote, you know thirty years ago. So I said well that’s comforting because I know that if you don’t like what I write about your current record I’m not going to hear from you until 2050.
